sentences.text: From 1 s after the isolation, the attacker sender had 0 frames on brDN in all 30 loop-arm isolations with a distinct attacker MAC (A1, A2, A5, A8, C2, C3; 5 each), while the matching control runs kept 216 to 78,218 frames; A3 replays carry the boundary clock's MAC and cannot be separated.
sentences.quote: Own count (python gzip+struct, no 04_WEB_SIMULATOR code). Isolations: 30 loop runs (A1,A2,A5,A8,C2,C3 x r13-r17) each with exactly 1 act ISOLATE_PTP_AT_PORT (t_act 2.08-3.13 s after T0). Attacker PTP frames on brDN at t >= t_act+1 s, loop arm: 0 in all 30 (last attacker frame 2-137 ms BEFORE t_act in every run). Matching control runs, same window, no upper bound: min 220 (C2 r15), max 79597 (A5 r16). With the control's own would_act+1 s: 220 to 79,605. Bounded to t <= T0+40 s: 205 to 73,436; t < T0+42.5 s: 219 to 78,815. A3: 0 frames from unprovisioned or GM MACs in all 10 A3 runs; replayed frames reuse provisioned MACs (BC 02:..:02 and RU MACs), so A3 cannot be separated.
sentences.problem: The loop-arm zeros, the 30 isolations, the 5-per-scenario split and A3 not being separable all agree. The control range '216 to 78,218' is not reproduced: my counts are 220 to 79,597 (no upper bound). No window bound I tried (T0+40, T0+42.5, would_act-based) gives 216 or 78,218, and the maximum exceeds 78,218. Time alignment: no wall-clock/monotonic anchor exists in the run directories (timeline.json holds monotonic times only; start.log has one line). I used the first BC Announce on brDN (pcap wall time) against bc.log 'v-bc-dn ... to MASTER' (monotonic). Cross-check against the rogue/rbc's own MASTER transition vs its first Announce: residual within ±1 ms in all 10 A1/A8 loop runs. Note: the citation says the counts were made by 04_WEB_SIMULATOR/ingest/extract.py; this check did not use that code.
